1. MarginPad — best free heatmap, no login

BEST FOR: everyday traders who want the picture without a paywall

The live heatmap, 18 per-coin liquidation maps (real events as bubbles + a price-level histogram) and a real-time liquidations feed from 9 exchanges are all free, with no account. Estimated cluster layers are clearly labelled as estimates, real events as real. Pairs with 65 per-coin liquidation calculators and a free paper trading terminal to act on what you see.

Honest cons: no multi-year archives, fewer venues than Coinglass, no institutional dashboards.

2. Coinglass — deepest data, if you pay

BEST FOR: professionals who need history and breadth

The category incumbent: widest venue coverage, multi-year archives, dozens of derivatives dashboards. If your work justifies the subscription, it is the most complete product.

Honest cons: advanced heatmap models and real-time refresh are behind the paid Prime plan, and API access runs $29-299/mo. See our full Coinglass comparison.

3. Hyblock Capital — orderflow power tool

BEST FOR: orderflow specialists

Liquidation levels are one layer of a serious orderflow suite (order book depth, positioning, sentiment). Strong product for traders who live in that world.

Honest cons: subscription-first with account required; overkill if you just want the liquidation picture.

4. CoinAnk — broad Coinglass-style alternative

BEST FOR: a second opinion on cluster maps

Similar shape to Coinglass with per-symbol liquidation maps and derivatives dashboards; useful as a cross-check.

Honest cons: paywalls on depth, and interface polish trails the leaders.

5. The Kingfisher — early mover on free access

BEST FOR: quick free looks at majors

Markets itself on free access to liquidation maps and calculators, and deserves credit for pushing the free angle early.

Honest cons: model-only (no real events feed), limited coin coverage, deeper features gated.

6. TradingView community scripts — heatmap on your chart

BEST FOR: TradingView natives

Community-built liquidation overlays draw estimated levels directly on your TradingView chart — convenient if that is where you already work.

Honest cons: pure leverage-formula estimates with no live event data, quality varies wildly by script, and good ones are often invite-only.

The one thing every vendor shares

Cluster heatmaps are models. Nobody outside an exchange knows where every position's liquidation actually sits, so every vendor — including the paid ones — estimates clusters from open interest changes and assumed leverage distributions. The honest differences between tools are: whether they also show real liquidation events (trades that actually happened), whether the model is labelled as a model, and what you pay to see it. That is the standard this list applies. One exception exists: on-chain venues like Hyperliquid publish real positions with exact liquidation prices — see our Hyperliquid whale tracker.

Are liquidation heatmaps real data or estimates?

Why do traders watch liquidation heatmaps?
